To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a Fe(III)-doped graphitic carbon nitride (CNF) was used to activate peroxymonocarbonate (PMS) for selective degradation of phenolic compounds via high-valent iron-oxy species.

the Fe(III)doped g-C3NS4 catalyst was capable of selectively removing phenolic compounds in a wide pH (3-9), which was ascribed to the high-valent ironoxo species fixtated in the nitrogen ports of the g-C3N 4.
the Fe(III)/CNF system was capable of effectively removing phenolic compounds in a wide pH (3-9), which was mainly due to the generation of ≡FeVO.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the selective degradation of phenolic compounds by PMS/CNF systems, which is of great significance for the practical application of PMS activation.
the development of an efficient heterogeneous PMS activation system, Fe(III)-doped g-C3n4, to selectively remove phenolic compounds in a wide pH (3-9).
a new peroxomonosulfate ( PMS) activation system using Fe(III)-doped g-C 3N 4 as the heterogeneous catalyst.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Fe(III)/g-C3N4/PMS system is capable of selectively degrating phenolic compounds via high-valent iron species in a wide pH region (3-9).
the Fe(III)/CNF3 system can effectively remove 4-CP via the nonradical pathway, which is attributed to the formation of high-valent iron species.
Fe(III)-doped g-C3 N4 (CNF3) was capable of effectively activating PMS to degrade phenolic compounds via high-valent iron-oxy species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PMS can be effectively activated by Fe(III)-doped g-C3n4 to selectively degrade phenols via nonradical oxidation pathway, which can be applied to treat wastewater containing phenolic compounds.
the PMS/CNFCatalytic system could be applied in the selective degradation of phenolic compounds in a broad pH range via high-valent ironoxo species.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Fe(III)/CNF catalyst can activate PMS to generate high-valent iron oxo radicals, which can be used to degrade organic pollutants in a wide pH environment.
the Fe(III)/g-C3N4 catalyst can be used to effectively activate PMS to degrade phenolic compounds via nonradical mechanism.
the Fe(III)/CNF3 system could activate PMS to generate high-valent iron-oxygen species for selective degradation of organic pollutants in a wide pH region.
